newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh says Burma refugees still refusing food.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh says Burma refugees still refusing food.

text.p: Bangladesh said on Wednesday that Burmese refugees who do not want to be sent home are still refusing to accept food rations offered by the government.

Many of the 21,000 Burmese refugees in Bangladesh, known as Rohingyas, began a food boycott on July 21 as part of a protest against what they believe are attempts by Bangladesh to send them home by force.

"Latest bids on Wednesday to persuade them to accept food rations have failed. They just turned down our offer and a plea by the UNHCR relief agency to accept it," Relief and Repatriation Commissioner Qamrul Huda said.
Huda, other government officials and Van To Nguyen of the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) spent three hours talking to the refugees at Nayapara camp.
"Like yesterday, the Rohingyas (Burmese Moslems) refused to budge from their stance," Huda told Reuters by telephone.
Clashes between police and Rohingyas resisting repatriation on July 20 left nearly 20 people injured, forcing authorities to postpone the repatriation from Nayapara and the other Kutupalong camp.

The relief and government officials said they reaffirmed to the refugees on Wednesday that Dhaka would not send anyone home against their will. But Bangladesh has said it will not allow any Rohingyas to stay permanently.
The refugees on Wednesday handed a list of demands to the government officials.
"They include permission for the Rohingyas in the refugee camps to stay in Bangladesh until democracy is restored in Myanmar (Burma)," one official said.
Van To, based in Cox's Bazar, said on Wednesday night that he saw no immediate solution to the crisis. "I see no immediate solution to the problem," he said.

The UNHCR earlier this month lodged a strong protest with the Bangladesh government over the alleged forcible deportation of the refugees from camps lining the highway from Cox's Bazar to Teknaf on Bangladesh's southernmost tip.
